research.title: Dead reckoning
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Estimating where you are": Your dashed plot is exactly that, and the switch that allows for the chart is the game's way of adding what a careful navigator would add.

research.title: Nautical mile
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "How long a nautical mile is": Every distance on the chart is in these miles, and every speed in these knots.

research.title: Chip log
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Where the knot comes from": Your speed and your time are all the game gives you, as they were all a navigator had.

research.title: Leeway
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Sliding sideways": In the game the slip is a fixed share of the wind across the ship, a simplification. The currents are charted as a set (the way they run) and a drift (how fast).

research.title: Magnetic declination
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "A compass that does not read true": The compass chapter prints one error as a range and asks you to steer the heading that is already corrected.

research.title: Marine chronometer
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Longitude and the clock": The game never asks you to find longitude from the stars; this is only a reminder of how hard knowing where you are once was.

other.title: Pyodide
other.note: Runs the game's Python rules in the browser through WebAssembly (version 0.26.4, loaded from a CDN), so the game needs no server of its own and no build step.
